HERIFORGE 2nd Open Call · Türkiye Hub · Challenge 1

The collection already knows. The export forgets.

VEKAM has published 200 objects from the Ankara Orchard House. Their curators recorded how each one was made, what it was used for, who used it, and in which century. When the collection is exported to Dublin Core for aggregation, 43% of what they wrote down is discarded — and it is precisely the part that describes living practice. This page is built from their real, public data.

The evidence

Which fields survive the export

Every field VEKAM's system declares a Dublin Core target for survives aggregation. Fields with no target are dropped silently. Sorted by how often curators filled them in.

FieldOn exportRecords filled FilledDistinct

The clearest case. Type survives as dc:type and carries one single value — “Obje” — for all 200 objects. Collection is dropped, and carries eight real classes: metal, textile, wood, ceramic, glass, carpet, organic, porcelain. The field that aggregates is empty of meaning; the field that classifies never leaves the building.

Object by object

What a record loses, and what it becomes

Pick any object. On the left is the record as it leaves VEKAM today. On the right is what the pipeline recovers, with the CIDOC CRM property each value is reconstructed into. Turkish is the curators' own wording, kept as recorded.

Why it matters

The practices are already in the data

Group the objects by the intended-use field — the one that is dropped — and living practices appear with no manual curation. The challenge asks for a minimum of three categories of intangible heritage linked to people, places, objects and time periods. Here are four, derived from existing records.

The technique vocabulary contains “Seyrek örgü” (5 objects) and “Seyrak örgü” (2 objects). One technique, two spellings, no controlled vocabulary to bind them. Reconciling terms against Getty AAT makes that a single concept with a stable URI — and makes the cluster above complete rather than nearly complete.

Provenance and method

Every record, field name and value on this page comes from Koç University Libraries / VEKAM, Ankara Bağ Evi Koleksiyonu (CONTENTdm collection ABE), read through the library's public API on 16 September 2026. Nothing is invented and nothing is simulated. The “dropped” classification is VEKAM's own field configuration: each field declares its Dublin Core target, and the fields counted as dropped are those the configuration leaves unmapped.

Thumbnails are loaded directly from the library's public IIIF server for display only; each object links back to its record at Koç University for the full image and authoritative metadata. English glosses are editorial aids for this demonstration — the Turkish values are authoritative. A production pipeline is bilingual throughout, as the challenge requires.

Reproduce the figures: python poc/harvest/harvest_abe.py then python poc/map/map_to_crm.py.
